validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed independently and repeatedly. Carolina Gas Transmission, LLC (CGT) is a live, FERC-regulated interstate natural gas pipeline company, confirmed via its current owner's corporate page (bhegts.com/our-businesses/CGT, accessed 2026-09-10) and via three SEC EDGAR filings spanning three different owners: SCANA Corp's FY2006 10-K (filed 2007-03-01), Dominion Midstream Partners LP's 8-K of 2014-12-17 announcing Dominion's purchase of CGT from SCANA, and Berkshire Hathaway Energy's 8-K of 2020-07-06 announcing the acquisition of Dominion's gas transmission business including 100% of Carolina Gas Transmission. These are independent origins (three different corporate filers, three different transactions, spanning 2006-2020) that all agree. CLASSIFICATION: correctly classified as gas transmission, not gathering -- SCANA's FY2006 10-K states CGTC 'operates an open access, transportation-only interstate pipeline company regulated by FERC,' and bhegts.com confirms 'high-pressure, interstate natural gas pipeline.' OWNERSHIP CHAIN verified with dates: South Carolina Pipeline Corp / SCG Pipeline merged Nov 1, 2006 to form Carolina Gas Transmission Corporation (SCANA subsidiary) -> Dominion Resources agreed to buy CGT from SCANA for ~$492.9M, announced 2014-12-16, closed Jan 2015 (Dominion Midstream Partners 8-K) -> Berkshire Hathaway Energy acquired 100% of CGT along with the rest of Dominion's GT&S business, announced 2020-07-06, expected to close Q4 2020 (BHE 8-K), matching bhegts.com's own history timeline (SCE&G 1952 -> SC Pipeline 1984 -> CGT 2006 -> Dominion 2015 -> BHE 2020). Owner1 as recorded ('Carolina Gas Transmission LLC' 100%) is the direct/legal owner of the FERC-jurisdictional assets (the operating subsidiary itself), consistent with how other clustered rows in this batch record the direct subsidiary rather than the ultimate parent (cf. Black Bear Transmission LLC / Project Tarpon Holdco note) -- I did not contest it. NOT A DUPLICATE: this is the aggregate SYSTEM row (1,500 mi, no Capacity/Diameter -- both correctly blank at network granularity) and is clearly distinct from the project-level segment rows in the same cluster (P4381 Columbia-to-Eastover 29 mi, P4382 Transco-to-Charleston 55 mi, P2649 Columbia-to-Eastover Gas Pipeline 45 km) which are individual laterals built onto the CGT system, not restatements of the whole network. GEOGRAPHY: the EndState/Province='Georgia' flagged in the batch brief as disagreeing with route geometry is CORRECT per two independent sources -- both bhegts.com ('markets in South Carolina and southeast Georgia') and the Dominion Midstream 2014-12-17 8-K ('CGT owns and operates nearly 1,500 miles of FERC-regulated interstate natural gas pipeline in South Carolina and southeastern Georgia') state the system extends into southeastern Georgia. The route-geometry mismatch noted in the brief is a gap in the mapped route (it evidently doesn't yet include the Georgia extent), not a defect in the sheet's state cells -- no route edit is in scope here, but worth flagging to whoever next touches P3221's route.
